description: MISSING --node ON THE STATE-CHANGING TXs AND ON keys show. The script exports AKASH_NODE (line 20) but the lease-create (line 86) and deployment-create (line 70) and `keys show` (line 24) do NOT pass --node; they rely on provider-services reading AKASH_NODE from the environment. provider-services honors the AKASH_NODE env var for query/tx in recent versions, but the bid query on line 77 EXPLICITLY passes --node while the txs do NOT — this inconsistency means if env-var resolution differs from --node (e.g. an older binary, or a flag-vs-env precedence quirk) the txs broadcast to the DEFAULT node (often a dead/wrong endpoint) while the query hits the right one. The deployment would then be created on a different node than the bids are queried from -> 'no dseq' or 'no bids'. send-manifest (line 88) talks to the provider directly (no --node needed) which is fine, but it is also missing -y/keyring consistency context.

evidence.snippet: tx deployment create ... (no --node)   vs   query market bid list ... --node "$AKASH_NODE"   vs   tx market lease create ... (no --node)

correctFix: Pass --node "$AKASH_NODE" --chain-id "$AKASH_CHAIN_ID" explicitly on EVERY query and tx (deployment create, bid list, lease create, keys show where relevant) for consistency, OR rely solely on env vars for all of them — do not mix. Relying on AKASH_NODE env alone is acceptable only if verified against the actual binary version pinned in B1.
